text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said in South Africa that his government's policies of being accountable, transparent, implementing correct economic policies and encouraging high savings and investment accounts for the city state's success.
- Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen said the reunification of Taiwan with China has become a more urgent mission for Beijing after the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
- Singapore will set in place a three-year rolling plan of technical cooperation with Botswana, Namibia, South Africa and Zimbabwe, Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said.

- A United States-Japan shipping war loomed larger yesterday after Washington levelled a fee of US$100,000 on Japanese cargo vessels for each call they make at a U.S. port from abroad, the U.S. Federal Maritime Commission said.
- Indonesian conglomerate Sinar Mas has found a second listed vehicle in the form of stationary maker Nippecraft.
- Stamp duty collections jumped almost 36 percent to Singapore $1.84 billion while property taxes slumped 12 percent to S$1.56 billion mainly as a result of last May's curbs on property speculation.
- Retailer Metro Holdings is diversifying into the luxury cruise business in the face of gloomy retail conditions.
- Retailer Metro Holdings has decided to diversify for the first time in 23 years by committing more than Singapore $88 million into the cruise and casino business.
- Indonesian congolmerate Sinar Mas is poised to snatch a second listed vehicle here through the acquisition of its unit of 64 percent of Nippecraft.

- Prices of residential properties along the East Coast of Singapore have been the hardest hit by the introduction of anti-speculation measures by the government last May, figures from the Singapore Institute of Surveyors and Valuers showed.
- The earnings outlook of electronic companies in Singapore looks brighter this year following the industry-wide slowdown in the first three nine months of 1996.
- Stockbroker GK Goh's net earnings for the six months to December 31 fell 1.7 percent to Singapore $8.9 million mainly due to the lacklustre performance of the equities market here.
- Commodity transportation provider Noble Group Ltd launched its initial public offering yesterday, confident that its Singapore listing would not flounder the way its Hong Kong listing did.
- Richard Li's Pacific Century Regional Development will buy a huge retail, residential and office complex being built in Beijing for US$113.7 million in cash, the company said.
